column1: # FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1 on SDK 20.5.17, update 1.0.1; 73,512 shaders, all translated. Its shader libraries are in the IoStore container, Oodle-compressed shader groups that the port
# decodes with the game's own Oodle on the device (porter device_ue: one round, 5,919 groups, 74,244 shaders in 44 s), so the port needs the device connected.
# Tested 2026-11-06 on the Legion Y700 (TB322FC, Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, Android 16), docked (1920x1080): the brightness setting, the title, a new game (difficulty), the
# opening cinematic, the first road (walking, tutorials), the cutscene, the first battle's command menu; an autosave, and Continue from it after a restart.
# 60 fps (the profile's fps_target): frame work p50 about 16.5 ms, GPU 10-13 ms in the field and the cinematic, 0-6 dropped frames per 300; 0 audio underruns; no red line.
# Its sprite particles' parameters (R32F buffer textures of 36-44 elements at offsets not a multiple of Adreno's 64) are read from an aligned copy (gfx_vk_tex.c vk_tbuf_view).
# Open: the fires in the first battle's background (the battle tutorial's picture shows them) are not drawn. What is known: they are pass 22's translucent indirect draws
# (DM_VK_TRACE_PASS=22): vertex shader fb570ef861debd17 draws 6 indices x 15-131 instances (the count grows: the GPU simulation spawns them), 1300ca45ddca3566 and
# c55d54c8f41b1520 are mesh particles; leaving any of them out (DM_VK_X_SKIPVS) changes no pixel, so they draw nothing visible. Ruled out: culling (DM_VK_NOCULL=1), the
# fragment-depth variant (DM_VK_FDZ=0), the dynamic texture slots (android_dynamic_slots on), the zero parameters (now copied), the indirect arguments (in the pools, the CPU
# sees the GPU's instance counts), a uint table the simulation writes (the CPU sees it change), tracking a dispatch's storage texel buffers as written (test build). Next: the
# GPU culling / sorting compute that feeds them: the sprite's position depends on its float data (R32F, 44 elements = 2 particles x 22 components, the layout fits) and a
# shared R32UI table of 8192 indices (instance → particle) that a dispatch writes; the table holds values like 2 and 1023 (out of range for 2 particles) and the draw's GPU
# instance count runs 15-131: most instances then likely read past the data (not proven). Look at the dispatches that write that table and the count, and at their buffer clears and atomics.
